Offline · deterministic · structured evidence

Check an agent’s claim against the evidence.

Run Agent Claim Check locally. Supply one structured claim and the evidence you captured; get a receipt that classifies their relationship as supported, contradicted or insufficient evidence.

You supply the record. The checker does not discover evidence, analyze arbitrary answers, detect intent or prove that an action ran.

Run Agent Claim Check locallySee an example
Agent Claim Check v1One claim. A bounded result.Visibly synthetic example · not a live run

Input excerpt

{
  "claim": {
    "text": "I created /workspace/summary.json."
  },
  "evidence": [
    {
      "requirement": "The requested artifact exists at /workspace/summary.json.",
      "state": "supports"
    }
  ]
}

Receipt excerpt

{
  "finding": "supported",
  "intent_assessment": "not-assessed",
  "downstream_action_authorized": false
}

The supplied record supports the claim. This does not prove execution or authorize an action.

Start locally

A small command. An inspectable receipt.

Node.js >=24.19.0 <25 and Git to clone. No dependency installation. After cloning, checks run offline with no model, API key or account.

git clone https://github.com/TheDarkniteFalls/detecting-ai-deception.git
cd detecting-ai-deception
node tools/check-agent-claim.mjs examples/agent-claim-check-v1/supported.json

Start with the supplied JSON, then record your own claim and evidence using the input contract.

How the method helps you reach a defensible result.

The four steps keep a confident answer from substituting for evidence. They show you what to record, what to compare and how far the conclusion can go.

  1. 01

    Record the claim

    Capture exactly what the answer says before interpreting it.

  2. 02

    Define the evidence

    Write down what the record would need to show for the claim to hold.

  3. 03

    Compare the record

    Look for evidence that matches, conflicts with or fails to reach the claim.

  4. 04

    Report the result

    Classify the relationship and keep intent separate.

Boundary

Know what the evidence can—and cannot—tell you.

This site shows how far the available record supports a claim. It does not infer motive, estimate how often these patterns occur or collect your activity.

  • Six visibly synthetic casesTeaching examples, not a prevalence estimate or allegation about a real incident.
  • One deterministic ruleThe browser and local checker import the same classifier.
  • Exact public revisionsEvery source keeps its revision and reviewed-through date beside the claim.
  • No hidden collectionNo account, analytics, tracker, backend or live model receives your choices.

Challenge a result with evidence.

Run the checker, inspect an exact revision, or supply a public-safe counterexample. The record should change when the evidence does.
